items.title: NIST shares feedback on AI-agent identity and authorisation
items.authors: NIST National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence
items.summary: NCCoE has published feedback on its agent-identity project and selected software development as the first implementation use case.
items.relevance: Relevant to attributing automated actions and limiting the authority of agents working inside an organisation.

items.title: New DevSecOps resources and an agentic-AI project update
items.authors: NIST National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence
items.summary: New resources connect secure-development practices with example pipelines and plans for agentic AI. The announcement also lists a webinar on 28 October 2026.
items.relevance: A practical connection between AI-agent research, identity controls, and secure software development.

items.title: Towards trustworthy cybersecurity: Reclassifying insider threat detection using SHAP
items.authors: Raddad Faqihi, Priyadarsi Nanda, Manoranjan Mohanty, Saleh Alqahtani and Bashair Alrashed
items.venue: Future Generation Computer Systems, volume 183, article 108543
items.summary: A study combining SHAP feature attributions with security-domain knowledge to support analyst-guided reclassification of insider-threat predictions. The reported evaluation uses CMU CERT data.
items.relevance: Connects explanation assessment with analyst judgement. Its CERT-based findings are a useful prompt for testing explanation quality and transfer beyond a single benchmark.

items.title: The CERT Dataset Decade: A Systematic Review of Methodological Evolution and Performance Bias
items.venue: Journal of Criminal Justice and Security
items.summary: A review of methodological limitations in machine-learning studies using CERT, including how evaluation choices affect the interpretation of reported performance.
items.relevance: Useful context for checking whether apparently comparable benchmark results answer the same research question.

items.title: The SPEDIA dataset
items.summary: A published dataset study combining behaviour collected in a controlled cyber exercise, simulated activity, and synthetic data derived from CERT.
items.relevance: A useful example of why dataset provenance matters when constructing independent transfer evaluations.

items.title: Attention is not Explanation
items.authors: Sarthak Jain and Byron C. Wallace
items.summary: Experiments on NLP models examine the relationship between attention weights and predictions, challenging the assumption that attention automatically explains a decision.
items.relevance: A methodological prompt for security researchers to test explanation faithfulness in their own model and task.

items.title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
items.summary: A study of how to evaluate saliency methods, showing why visually convincing explanations alone are insufficient evidence of reliability.
items.relevance: A starting point for designing checks of whether an explanation depends on what a model has learned.
